title: 'Nobody owns me': Poncho Casso tells Laredo contractors City Hall is 'anti business' in 10-minute campaign speech
excerpt: Mayoral candidate Alfonso 'Poncho' Casso told Laredo's electrical and mechanical contractors the building department is weaponized against City Hall's critics, claimed credit for Sheriff Martin Cuellar's indictment, and urged an early-vote turnout he says will decide Nov. 3.
content:
Mayoral candidate Alfonso "Poncho" Casso took his campaign directly to Laredo's construction trades this week, telling a room of electrical and mechanical contractors that City Hall's building department is "anti business," that licensing laws go unenforced while unlicensed operators take their work, and that no donor owns his campaign.

The roughly 10-minute speech, delivered before the MEP contractors — the mechanical and electrical contractors of Laredo — was posted to Casso's Facebook page on the night of Oct. 20, the second day of early voting in the Nov. 3 mayoral election. Early voting runs Oct. 19–30.

Casso told the contractors the building department has been weaponized against people City Hall dislikes while favored operators get a pass, and that the city fails to enforce licensing rules, allowing unlicensed operators to undercut licensed firms. He also alleged that businesses face demands for a "mordida" — a bribe — an allegation he did not document in the speech. "City Hall doesn't care about the people," he said. Webb Watch 956 presents these as the candidate's claims; the city has not responded to them in the speech, and no findings were offered.

He cast himself as an outsider with a record, recalling that he was elected to the City Council in 1994 at age 38, built a five-vote coalition within two years, fired the city manager and forced out department heads. He described himself as the least-funded candidate in the race who refuses big money, saying "nobody owns me" and alleging that rival candidates are "bought and paid for by either the banks or development companies." That is his allegation about his opponents; he named no specific transaction.

Casso also claimed credit for the federal indictment of Webb County Sheriff Martin Cuellar. He told the contractors he was the witness who spoke to the FBI carrying what he called a "smoking gun document," said he had actually been pursuing a UISD board member, and called the sheriff "collateral damage." He said he filed the lawsuit seeking the sheriff's removal. Webb Watch 956 notes the distinction: Casso did file a court petition seeking Cuellar's removal — that is a matter of public record. His claimed role in the federal indictment is his own account and has not been independently verified. The indictment itself is an allegation; Sheriff Cuellar is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

The candidate also attacked council compensation, calling council pensions illegal and unethical. By his figures, council members made about $6,000 a year in his era versus roughly $80,000 now, and the mayor about $111,000 plus a $1,200 monthly car allowance and an $85,000 Denali with bulletproof windows and a chauffeur. Those figures are Casso's, presented here as he stated them.

Looking ahead, Casso urged the room to vote early, arguing that whoever gets the most votes in early voting is going to win. He said he expects a runoff is possible — mentioning fellow candidates Alyssa Cigarroa and JD Gonzalez — but believes he can win outright on Nov. 3. He warned rivals, "you hit me and I'm going to hit you back so hard," and lamented that Laredo is falling behind McAllen and losing its young people to other cities.

Casso is one of five candidates seeking to unseat Mayor Victor D. Treviño on Nov. 3. Webb Watch 956 is covering every candidate's public campaign statements on the same terms, and will report responses from City Hall, the mayor's office, or the other campaigns as they are received.

Sources: Campaign speech video posted by Alfonso "Poncho" Casso, Facebook, Oct. 20, 2026; Webb County election calendar — early voting Oct. 19–30, 2026, Election Day Nov. 3, 2026.
